name: Vienna
tagline: Imperial palaces, music and coffee houses
summary: Mix one palace, one museum and one coffee house per day. The Ring boulevard holds most sights, and Schönbrunn needs a half day of its own.
seasonNote: December Christmas markets are a peak; January and February are cold and quiet.
arrival: The S7 train and the City Airport Train reach the centre in 16 to 25 minutes.
gettingAround: The U-Bahn and trams are excellent; a 24 to 72 hour pass is good value.
cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but some coffee houses, sausage stands and markets prefer cash.
foodTip: Have a Wiener schnitzel, a Käsekrainer from a sausage stand and cake with a melange.
buyTip: Chocolates and Sachertorte to take home, Augarten porcelain and Manner wafers.
baseArea: Inside or just outside the Ring; Neubau for a local feel

connections.note: Direct Railjet trains every two hours.

items.name: Schönbrunn Palace
items.summary: The Habsburgs' summer palace: gilded state rooms and formal gardens climbing to the Gloriette.
items.expect: Timed palace tickets that sell out by midday in season.
items.tip: Book online; the gardens are free and the Gloriette has the view.

It is Austria's most visited sight and the full picture of imperial life.

items.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral
items.summary: The Gothic cathedral at the city's centre, with a patterned tile roof and climbable towers.
items.expect: Free to enter the back; the nave, towers and catacombs are ticketed.
items.tip: Climb the 343 steps of the south tower for the roof view.

items.expect: Seats sell out; cheap standing tickets go on sale on the day.
items.tip: Try for standing-room tickets, or take the 40-minute guided tour.

items.tip: Reserve online, and order potato salad on the side.
